STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r5.claim: After brief mention of Moses and Jesus, the surah discusses humanity's tendency to divide into religious groups.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r5.anchor: Brief mention of Moses and Jesus follows, after which the sūrah dwells upon the human tendency to divide into religious groups (vv. 42–54)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ELMALILI:23:42-50/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:42-50/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:42-50/r3.claim: Pharaoh’s people reject two humans like themselves, claiming that the prophets’ people serve them.
ELMALILI:23:42-50/r3.anchor: Hâlbuki onların kavmi bize kulluk ediyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r2.claim: Before Moses led them out, the Israelites had lived in Egypt for four centuries as second-class citizens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r2.anchor: İsrâiloğulları, Hz. Mûsâ kendilerini Mısır’dan çıkarmadan önce dört asırdır Mısır’da yaşıyor, burada ikinci sınıf vatandaş muamelesi görüyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r3.claim: Pharaoh and his entourage regarded the Israelites as their slaves and argued that accepting the religion of Moses and Aaron, who came from the same people, would dishonor them; their arrogant pride led to their destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r3.anchor: Firavun ve çevresinin bu sebeple onları kendi köleleri gibi gördükleri, dolayısıyla aynı kavimden olan Mûsâ ve Hârûn’un dinlerini kabul etmenin kendileri için onur kırıcı olacağını ileri sürdükleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r4.claim: The story warns Meccan pagans and all people that judging right and wrong by status, wealth, or lineage brings a severe cost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:45/r4.anchor: doğru ve yanlışı makam-mevki, mal-mülk, soy-sop gibi ölçülerle ayırmaya kalkışmaları halinde bunun bedelinin çok ağır olacağı uyarısında bulunulmaktadır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r3.claim: The history of messengers and rejecters in this section demonstrates believers' success and the fate of deniers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r3.anchor: The purpose is to prove in the light of history the premise that is mentioned: success of the believers and the fate of those have rejected the truth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r4.claim: God's established practice dooms those who deny His messengers; their worldly respite is a trial and tightens their noose despite appearing successful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r4.anchor: those who deny God’s messenger will be doomed eternally; however, since God makes the wrongdoers undergo a trial in this world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r5.claim: The preceding sūrah briefly recounts messenger stories, while this passage treats them in more detail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r5.anchor: Verses 42-45 of the previous sūrah also mention the anecdotes of God’s messengers and their rejecters. However, it is very brief.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r6.claim: Noah is the only earlier messenger named; among later messengers Moses, Aaron, and Jesus are named, while the others remain unnamed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p249/r6.anchor: by name only Noah (sws) is mentioned among the earlier messengers and Moses (sws), Aaron (sws) and Jesus (sws) among the later ones.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p262/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p262/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p262/r2.claim: The plural verb is used in agreement with the collective 'nation' in Pharaoh and his people's statement that the two messengers' people are their slaves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p262/r2.anchor: is used in deference to the word “nation” that has been mentioned earlier in the statement of the Pharaoh and his people

BURSEVI:v6p61/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p61/r4.claim: Their response is grammatically joined to their arrogance, with the intervening phrase serving as a parenthetical confirmation; they spoke among themselves as if advising one another.
BURSEVI:v6p61/r4.anchor: عطف على استكبروا وما بينهما اعتراض مقرر للاستكبار أي قالوا فيما بينهم بطريق المناصحة

BURSEVI:v6p61/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p61/r5.claim: The interrogative in “shall we believe?” is a denial: they mean that they will not believe and that belief should not issue from them.
BURSEVI:v6p61/r5.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار بمعنى لا نؤمن وما ينبغي أن يصدر منا الإيمان

BURSEVI:v6p61/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p61/r6.claim: The dual description “like us” uses a form treated as a general verbal noun that applies to singular, dual, and plural, masculine and feminine.
BURSEVI:v6p61/r6.anchor: وصف بالمثل الاثنان لأنه في حكم المصدر العام للإفراد والتثنية والجمع المذكر والمؤنث

BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r1.claim: “Their people” means the Children of Israel; they are described as Pharaoh’s servants and dependents, as though enslaved, which the speakers use to lower Moses’ and Aaron’s standing below prophethood.

BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r2.claim: The speakers meant to diminish the two messengers’ high rank by pointing to their people’s subordination to Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r2.anchor: قصدوا بذلك التعرض لشأنهما وحط رتبتهما العلية عن منصب الرسالة

BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r3.claim: Kashifi relays a report found in some commentaries that the Children of Israel worshipped Pharaoh; the gloss says that such obedience would count as worship in reality.
BURSEVI:v6p61#2/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در بعضى تفاسير آورده انده كه بني إسرائيل فرعون رامي رستيدند

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r3.claim: بشر can denote one person or a group, so its dual form لبشرين is valid; مثل can describe singular, dual, or plural nouns of either gender without necessarily changing form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r3.anchor: والبشر يطلق على المفرد والجمع كقوله فإما ترين من البشر أحدا ولما أطلق على الواحد جازت تثنيته فلذلك جاء لبشرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r4.claim: Their claim that the two messengers' people were their servants refers to the Children of Israel and means they were subdued and humiliated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r4.anchor: وقومهما أي بنو إسرائيل لنا عابدون أي خاضعون فتذللون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r5.claim: Another explanation is that Pharaoh claimed divinity, so the people really worshipped him; alternatively, Abū ʿUbayd says Arabs call anyone subject to a king a worshipper.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p565/r5.anchor: أو لأنه كان يدعي الإلهية فادعى الناس العبادة، وأن طاعتهم له عبادة على الحقيقة. وقال أبو عبيد: العرب تسمي كل من دان للملك عابدا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.claim: The clause ‘so they said’ coordinates with their arrogance; the intervening phrase explains it, and they spoke among themselves as if advising one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.anchor: عطف على ( استكبروا ) وما بينهما اعتراض مقرر للإستكبار والمراد فقالوا فيما بينهم بطريق المناصحة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.claim: Bashar can be singular or collective, but it is dual here; mithl is singular because it functions like a verbal noun, though both forms can elsewhere be dual or plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.anchor: ثنى البشر لأنه يطلق على الواحد كقوله تعالى ( بشرا سويا ) ويطلق على الجمع كما في قوله تعالى ( فأما ترين من البشر أحدا )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.claim: The dual for the two messengers highlights their fewness and separation from the many chiefs; the singular ‘like us’ stresses their complete resemblance, as if they were one.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.anchor: إلا أن المرجح لتثنيته الأول وإفراد الثاني الإشارة بالأول إلى قلتها وانفرادهما عن قومهما مع كثرة الملأ واجتماعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r4.claim: These stories expose the deniers’ mistaken analogy between prophets and themselves; human nature ranges from prophets’ purified souls and sacred power to ignorant people who are worse than cattle.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r4.anchor: وهذه القصص كما ترى تدل على أن مدار شبه المنكرين للنبوة قياس حال الأنبياء عليهم السلام على أحوالهم بناء على جهلهم بتفاصيل شؤن الحقيقة البشرية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r5.claim: Prophets’ pure souls connect them to both subtle and material worlds, enabling them to receive revelation and guide others without neglecting human needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r5.anchor: بحيث يكون بعضها أعلى عليين وهم المختصون بالنفوس الزكية المؤيدون بالقوة القدسية المتعلقون لصفاء جواهرهم بكلا العالمين اللطيف والكثيف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r6.claim: The author marvels that they rejected a human prophet while many accepted a stone as divine, and reads the interrogative hamza as denial: ‘we will not believe.’
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#2/r6.anchor: ومن العجب أنهم لم يرضوا للنبوة ببشر وقد رضي أكثرهم للإلهية بحجر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r1.claim: An objection says the speech appears to come from Pharaoh’s chiefs, which weighs against taking ‘servants’ as actual worshippers; speaking in the king’s voice is possible but strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r1.anchor: واعترض بأن الظاهر أن هذا القول من الملأ وهو يأبى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r2.claim: Even if Pharaoh spoke and claimed divinity, that does not entail that Israelites actually worshipped him or that he claimed they did; reports say he often displayed the opposite of what he concealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r2.anchor: لا يلزم من ادعائه الإلهية عبادة بني إسرائيل له أو كونه يعتقد أو يدعي عبادتهم على الحقيقة له

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r3.claim: The author prefers ‘servants’ as a sense that fits Pharaoh and his chiefs, who meant to disparage the two messengers and lower their rank apart from their human nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r3.anchor: نعم الأولى تفسير ( عابدون ) بخادمون وهو مما يصح إسناده إلى فرعون وملئه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r4.claim: The preposed ‘to us’ phrase attaches to ‘servants’; it may be fronted for rhyme or restriction, meaning they serve us rather than the messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r4.anchor: واللام في ( لنا ) متعلقة بعابدون قدمت عليه رعاية للفواصل وقيل للحصر أي لنا عابدون لا لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r5.claim: The clause is circumstantial and reinforces their refusal through a false analogy between religious and worldly leadership, which they think rests on wealth and social status.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r5.anchor: والجملة حال من فاعل ( نؤمن ) مؤكدة لإنكار الإيمان لهما بناء على زعمهم الفاسد المؤسس على قياس الرياسة الدينية على الرياسة الدنيوية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r6.claim: Quraysh made a similar demand that revelation come to a great man from one of the two towns; the deniers ignored that God selects messengers for their noble qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p36#3/r6.anchor: كدأب قريش حيث قالوا : ( لو لا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r3.claim: Pharaoh and his people ask whether they should believe two men like themselves, meaning Moses and Aaron, while their people are submissive to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r3.anchor: يعني: موسى وهارون، {وقومهما لنا عابدون} مطيعون متذللون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r4.claim: Arabic calls anyone who submits to a king an ʿābid of that king.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p419/r4.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل من دان للملك: عابدا له

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r5.claim: “Two humans” is dual because bashar can be used for one person, as in Mary, or for a group; mithl is not dual because it functions like a verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r5.anchor: ثنى البشر لأنه يطلق للواحد كقوله { بشرا سويا } كما يطلق للجمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r6.claim: The objectors' main argument against prophethood is the flawed analogy between prophets and themselves based on shared humanity; human capacities vary greatly, so exceptionally gifted people can know what others cannot.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r6.anchor: قصارى شبه المنكرين للنبوة قياس حال الأنبياء على أحوالهم لما بينهم من المماثلة في الحقيقة

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r7.claim: Some people are so deficient that thought yields them nothing, while at the other extreme people may need little study and perceive what others cannot; this is the point of the verse about a human messenger who receives revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r7.anchor: يمكن أن يكون في طرف الزيادة أغنياء عن التفكر والتعلم في أكثر الأشياء وأغلب الأحوال

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r8.claim: “Their people” means the Children of Israel, and “servants to us” means attendants who are obedient and submissive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:45-47/r8.anchor: يعني بني إسرائيل. { لنا عبدون } خادمون منقادون كالعباد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r5.claim: They rejected the messengers because they were human like themselves and because their peoples were enslaved to Pharaoh's court, which they treated as proof of superiority.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r6.claim: The author's counterargument is that people plainly differ greatly in knowledge and ability; if such differences are possible, humanity alone cannot disqualify a messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p202/r6.anchor: لما جعلوا هذا شبهة لم يجعوا عجزهم

DURR-FULL:v6p99/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r2.claim: Qatāda says Mary bore Jesus without a father.
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية} قال: ولدته مريم من غير أب هو له

DURR-FULL:v6p99/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas interprets the sign made of Jesus and his mother as a lesson.
DURR-FULL:v6p99/r3.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس رضي الله عنه في قوله {وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية} قال: عبرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r4.claim: The claim about believing in two humans explains their arrogance; it was spoken by some members of the elite to one another, then attributed to all because they had agreed on it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r4.anchor: وهذا ليس من قول فرعون ولكنه قول بعض الملإ لبعض ، ولما كانوا قد تراوضوا عليه نسب إليهم جميعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r5.claim: Pharaoh listened to their counsel but had a separate declaration, that he knew no deity for them but himself; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he was treated as a deity, though human in appearance, as a son of gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r5.anchor: وأما فرعون فكان مصغيا لرأيهم ومشورتهم وكان له قول آخر حكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r6.claim: Their question is a denial: they deemed themselves unable to believe in two humans like them, since the messengers refuted the divinity of the idols they served.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r7.claim: Misguided elites demanded that a messenger differ in kind from those addressed, imagining hybrid bodily forms for their gods while ignoring the greater distinctions of soul and intellect; this fallacy led many nations to reject messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p63/r7.anchor: فكان ملأ فرعون لضلالهم يتطلبون لصحة الرسالة عن الله أن يكون الرسول مباينا للمرسل إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r1.claim: The lām after āman is transitive when someone is believed because of trust in the speaker; its original force is causal, as in the examples from al-ʿAnkabūt and al-Dukhān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r1.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لبشرين } لتعدية فعل { نؤمن } . يقال للذي يصدق المخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r2.claim: Āmantu bi-Muḥammad means believing the content or message, while āmantu li-Muḥammad means trusting Muhammad about what he brought; one says āman bi-Allāh, not āman li-Allāh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r2.anchor: ومعنى الأول يتعلق بذاته وهو الرسالة ومعنى الثاني أنك صدقته فيما جاء به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r3.claim: Mithlana may remain masculine singular despite its dual feminine noun, or agree with its noun, as in al-Aʿrāf 7:194.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r3.anchor: دون نظر إلى مخالفة صيغه موصوفه كما هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r4.claim: After attacking the messengers’ humanity, the elites attack their origins: their people are allegedly servants of the elites and thus inferior, so the messengers should not rule them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p64/r4.anchor: وهذا طعن في رسالتهما من جانب حالهما الذاتي ثم أعقبوه بطعن من جهة منشئهما وقبيلهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p65/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p65/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p65/r1.claim: ʿĀbidūn means obedient and submissive; the Israelites had been servants and laborers for the Copts, as in al-Shuʿarāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p65/r1.anchor: وقوله : { عابدون } جمع عابد ، أي مطيع خاضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r7.claim: Their statement that the two peoples were servants means the peoples were subdued and humiliated; a path called muʿabbad is likewise one made level and submissive.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r8.claim: One account explains why the Arabs of al-Ḥīra were called al-ʿIbād: they entered the obedience of Khosrow.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#3/r8.anchor: ومن هنا قيل لعرب الحيرة العباد لأنهم دخلوا من بين العرب في طاعة كسرى، هذا أحد القولين في تسميتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r1.claim: God sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his council with compelling signs, proofs, and decisive arguments.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه بعث رسوله موسى، عليه السلام، وأخاه هارون إلى فرعون وملئه، بالآيات والحجج الدامغات، والبراهين القاطعات،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s people were too arrogant to follow and obey the two messengers because they were human, repeating earlier nations’ rejection of human messengers; their hearts were alike.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p475#3/r2.anchor: وأن فرعون وقومه استكبروا عن اتباعهما، والانقياد لأمرهما، لكونهما بشرين كما أنكرت الأمم الماضية بعثة الرسل من البشر، تشابهت قلوبهم،

JISHUMI:v7p5051/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5051/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5051/r11.claim: Bashar means a human, named for exposed skin, unlike animals covered in hair or wool.
JISHUMI:v7p5051/r11.anchor: والبشر: الإنسان، سمي بذلك لانكشاف بشرته بخلاف غيره، وفي الحيوانات المغطى بالشعر والصوف.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r5.claim: The Israelites who served Pharaoh were obedient to him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r6.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r6.claim: Their service to Pharaoh means they were submissive to him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r7.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r7.claim: Their service to Pharaoh means they were enslaved or held in subjection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the Children of Israel worshipped Pharaoh, while Pharaoh worshipped idols.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p55/r8.anchor: كان بنو إسرائيل يعبدون فرعون وكان فرعون يعبد الأصنام

MUQATIL:23:45-50/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:45-50/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:45-50/r3.claim: They objected to believing two ordinary human beings with no superiority over them, while the two men's people, Israel, were their servants.
MUQATIL:23:45-50/r3.anchor: { فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا } يعني أنصدق إنسانين مثلنا ليس لهما علينا فضل { وقومهما } يعني بنى إسرائيل { لنا عابدون } [آية: 47]

NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r1.claim: Bashar can be singular or collective, and mithl and ghayr can describe dual or plural forms and either gender.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r1.anchor: البشر يكون واحد جميعا ومثل وغير يوصف بهما الاثنان والجمع والمذكر والمؤنث

NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r2.claim: Their people are the Israelites, whom Pharaoh's people regarded as subject and obedient; in Arab usage, one who submits to a king is called his worshipper.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p123#6/r2.anchor: أى بنو إسرائيل ﴿ لنا عابدون ﴾ خاضعون مطيعون وكل من دان الملك فهو عابد له عند العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:23:45-48/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:45-48/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:45-48/r2.claim: The objection ‘shall we believe two humans like us’ was discussed earlier, without further explanation here.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:45-48/r2.anchor: { فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا } الآية، تقدم أيضا.

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the signs given to Moses were nine: staff, hand, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, the sea's parting, drought years, and reduced fruits.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هي الآيات التسع وهي العصا واليد والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم وانفلاق البحر والسنون والنقص من الثمرات

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets “Our signs” as God's religion; if both signs and clear authority meant miracles, the verse would redundantly coordinate one thing with itself.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن قوله : { بئاياتنا } أي بديننا واحتج بأن المراد بالآيات لو كانت هي المعجزات والسلطات المبين أيضا هو المعجز

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's view because signs mentioned in accounts of messengers mean miracles.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r3.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول لأن لفظ الآيات إذا ذكر في الرسل فالمراد منها المعجزات

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r4.claim: One answer is that the clear authority may be Moses's staff, singled out because it encompassed many miracles, including becoming a serpent, swallowing sorcery, splitting the sea, and producing springs.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r4.anchor: أن المراد بالسلطان المبين يجوز أن يكون أشرف معجزاته وهو العصا لأنه قد تعلقت بها معجزات شتى من انقلابها حية وتلقفها ما أفكته السحرة وانفلاق البحر

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r5.claim: A second answer is that the signs are the miracles, while the clear authority is their powerful demonstration of Moses's truth and stature.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون المراد بالآيات نفس تلك المعجزات وبالسلطان المبين كيفية دلالتها على الصدق

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r6.claim: A third answer makes the clear authority Moses's dominance in proving the Creator's existence and prophethood, while his opponents regarded him as worthless.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r6.anchor: سلام عليهم في الاستدلال على وجود الصانع وإثبات النبوة وأنه ما كان يقيم لهم قدرا ولا وزنا

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r7.claim: Moses's miracles also belonged to Aaron: as their prophethood was shared, so were their miracles.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r7.anchor: الآية تدل على أن معجزات موسى عليه السلام كانت معجزات هرون عليه السلام أيضا ، وأن النبوة كما أنها مشتركة بينهما فكذلك المعجزات

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r8.claim: Pharaoh and his people were characterized by arrogance and disdain; their being high-ranking may mean worldly status or power through numbers and strength.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r8.anchor: الاستكبار والأنفة والثاني : أنهم كانوا قوما عالين أي رفيعي الحال في أمور الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r9.claim: Al-Kashshāf notes that the concise dual phrasing avoids “like the two of us” and “peoples like them”; Arabs favor brevity, as in 4:140 and 3:110.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r9.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) لم يقل مثلينا كما قال : { إنكم إذا مثلهم } ( النساء : 14 ) ولم يقل أمثالهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r10.claim: Their objection had two parts: Moses and Aaron were human, and their people were subject to Pharaoh's group as servants or slaves.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r10.anchor: والشبهة مبنية على أمرين : أحدهما : كونهما من البشر وقد تقدم الجواب عنه والثاني : أن قوم موسى وهرون كانوا كالخدم والعبيد لهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says Arabs call anyone who obeys a king his ʿābid, or servant.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة العرب تسمى كل من دان لملك عابدا له

RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r12.claim: Another possibility is that Pharaoh claimed divinity and called people his worshippers because their obedience was truly worship.
RAZI-FULL:v23p89/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال إنه كان يدعي الإلهية فادعى أن الناس عباده وأن طاعتهم له عبادة على الحقيقة

STUDYQURAN:23:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r1.claim: “Slaves” denotes Egyptians’ literal ownership of Israelites and evokes the subservience Pharaoh demanded as worship, as in 79:24.
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r1.anchor: the Egyptians literally owned the Israelites—but it also evokes the worshipful attitude expected from the underlings

STUDYQURAN:23:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s and his people’s disdain echoes the notables of Noah’s community in 23:34.
STUDYQURAN:23:47/r2.anchor: The disdain expressed by Pharaoh and his people echoes that in the words spoken by the notables of Noah’s community

SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r1.claim: Bashar can denote one, two, or a group, masculine or feminine; it can also agree in number, as it does here, and in the example from 3:47.
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r1.anchor: قوله: { لبشرين }: " بشر " يقع على الواحد والمثنى والمجموع والمذكر والمؤنث

SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r2.claim: Mathalun remains singular and masculine because it behaves like a verbal noun, though it can agree with dual or plural referents, as in 3:13 and 47:38.
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r2.anchor: وأما إفراد " مثلنا " فلأنه يجري مجرى المصادر في الإفراد والتذكير

SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r3.claim: One explanation is that the intended likeness concerns being human, not number; another says the single form stands for two.
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r3.anchor: وقيل: أريد المماثلة في البشرية لا الكمية. وقيل: اكتفي بالواحد عن الاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r4.claim: Wa-qawhumā lanā ʿābidūn is a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:23:47/r4.anchor: قوله: { وقومهما لنا عابدون } جملة حالية

TABATABAI:23:44-49/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r15.claim: By calling Moses and Aaron ordinary men, Pharaoh's people deny that the brothers have superiority; they regard their own mastery over the brothers' people as proof of their own rank.
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r15.anchor: المراد بكونهما بشرين مثلهم نفي أن يكون لهما فضل عليهم، وبكون قومهما لهم عابدين فضلهم عليهما

TABATABAI:23:44-49/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r16.claim: Their reasoning implies that Moses should worship them rather than ask them to believe, as Pharaoh's threat to imprison Moses also illustrates.
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r16.anchor: كما قال فرعون لموسى { لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين }

TABRISI:23:45-50/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:45-50/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:45-50/r5.claim: Their objection was that Moses and Aaron were merely two humans, created as they were.
TABRISI:23:45-50/r5.anchor: أي أنصدق لإنسانين خلقهم مثل خلقنا

TABRISI:23:45-50/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:45-50/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:45-50/r6.claim: Bashar denotes a human with exposed skin, unlike animals covered with wool, feathers, or other covering; this is divine kindness because animals cannot reason out how to cover themselves, while humans can.
TABRISI:23:45-50/r6.anchor: ويسمى الإنسان بشرا لانكشاف بشرته وهي جلدته الظاهرة حتى احتاج إلى لباس يكنه وغيره من الحيوان مغطى البشرة بصوف أو ريش أو غيره لطفا من الله سبحانه بخلقه

TABRISI:23:45-50/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:45-50/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:45-50/r7.claim: Their claim that Moses and Aaron’s people served them means those people obeyed them like slaves obey their master.

TABRISI:23:45-50/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:45-50/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:23:45-50/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Israelites served Pharaoh, while Pharaoh worshipped idols.
TABRISI:23:45-50/r8.anchor: قال الحسن: كان بنو إسرائيل يعبدون فرعون وفرعون يعبد الأوثان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil explain the objection as refusing to believe two ordinary flesh-and-blood humans with no superiority over them; their people are the Children of Israel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: أنصدق إنسانين مثلنا من لحم ودم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says قومهما refers to the Children of Israel and لنا عابدون means obedient to us.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r2.anchor: {وقومهما} يعني بني إسرائيل. {لنا عابدون} قال ابن عباس: مطيعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says Arabs call a subject of a king عابدا and cites the people of al-Hira, subjects of Persian kings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: العرب تسمي كل من دان لملك عابدا له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines عابد as obedient and submissive, deriving عبد from it; in 19:44, do not serve Satan means do not obey him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p593#2/r4.anchor: وقال المبرد: العابد: المطيع والخاضع، ومنه اشتق العبد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:47/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:47/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:47/r1.claim: The Egyptians were obedient and submissive to Pharaoh's people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:47/r1.anchor: وقومهما لنا عابدون } أي: مطيعون متذللون

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401#2/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401#2/r9.claim: Pharaoh's people said they would believe two humans like themselves only if the messengers were angels; they meant Moses and Aaron.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401#2/r9.anchor: قوله: {فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا} [المؤمنون: 47] أي: أنصدق بشرين مثلنا، فلو كانا ملكين لآمنا بهما. يعنون موسى وهارون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p402/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p402/r1.claim: “Their people” means the Children of Israel; “servants to us” means Pharaoh's people enslaved them and imposed tribute, not that Israel worshipped them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p402/r1.anchor: {وقومهما} [المؤمنون: 47] يعنون بني إسرائيل. {لنا عابدون} [المؤمنون: 47] وكانوا قد استعبدوا بني إسرائيل، ووضعوا عليهم الجزية. وليس يعني أنهم يعبدوننا.

BURHAN:v2p328/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p328/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p328/r1.claim: An interrogative may be used by someone who already knows and seeks no information; it then functions rhetorically rather than as a genuine question.
BURHAN:v2p328/r1.anchor: قد يخرج الاستفهام عن حقيقته بان يقع ممن يعلم ويستغني عن طلب الافهام

BURHAN:v2p328/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p328/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p328/r2.claim: Report-like interrogatives divide into denial, which seeks the addressee's rejection, and affirmation, which seeks admission.
BURHAN:v2p328/r2.anchor: فالوارد للنفي يسمى استفهام انكار والوارد للاثبات يسمى استفهام تقرير

BURHAN:v2p328/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p328/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p328/r3.claim: The Thamud-like objection in this verse is a denial: they mean that they will not believe in two humans like themselves.
BURHAN:v2p328/r3.anchor: فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا وقومهما لنا عابدون

ITQAN:v3p211#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r1.claim: Istifhām is a request for understanding and is equivalent to istikhbār.
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r1.anchor: من أقسام الإنشاء الاستفهام وهو طلب الفهم وهو بمعنى الاستخبار

ITQAN:v3p211#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris distinguishes the terms: istikhbār is the first question, while istifhām is asking again after the first answer was not fully understood.
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r2.anchor: وقيل الاستخبار ما سبق أولا ولم يفهم حق الفهم فإذا سألت عنه ثانيا كان استفهاما حكاه ابن فارس

ITQAN:v3p211#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r3.speaker: ابن مالك
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mālik lists the interrogative tools and says all except hamza substitute for it; a real question requires a doubter who believes an answer can be known.
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مالك في المصباح وما عدا الهمزة نائب عنها ولكونه طلب ارتسام صورة ما في الخارج في الذهن

ITQAN:v3p211#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r4.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r4.claim: Some authorities say interrogative wording in God’s speech means the addressee already knows the affirmation or denial; elsewhere it can be figurative, and al-Ṣaffār is wrong to restrict that usage to hamza.
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الأئمة وما جاء في القرآن على لفظ الاستفهام فإنما يقع في خطاب الله على معنى أن المخاطب عنده علم

ITQAN:v3p211#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r5.claim: The first rhetorical use of interrogation is denial: the question means they do not believe in two humans like themselves.
ITQAN:v3p211#2/r5.anchor: ومنه ﴿ أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون ﴾ ﴿ أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا ﴾ أي لا نؤمن
